note_claims.claim: Panic attacks for 4 years.
Recurrent panic attacks with palpitations, breathlessness, hand tingling and fear of dying.
Panic attacks last about 10 minutes.
Frequency of attacks is now two to three times a week and increasing.
Associated symptoms include anticipatory anxiety and generalised worry.
Avoids supermarkets and the Underground.
Sleep is satisfactory.
Mood is 'fed up' but not depressed.
Reports thoughts of self-harm.
Caffeine intake is about six coffees a day (initially stated as four).
Alcohol intake is a couple of glasses of wine at the weekend.
No drug use.
Works in marketing; no time off.
Partner is off work with stress and has his own GP appointment.
Thyroid function was normal last month.
No regular medications or known drug allergies.
GAD-7 score is 15.
PHQ-9 score is 8.
Panic disorder with agoraphobic avoidance and generalised anxiety symptoms.
No risk to self identified.
Self-referral details for NHS Talking Therapies (CBT).
Start Sertraline 25 mg once daily for 1 week, then increase to 50 mg once daily; warned of possible initial increase in anxiety.
Review in 2 weeks after starting sertraline.
Reduce caffeine gradually.
If thoughts of self-harm, call NHS 111 (mental health option) or Samaritans on 116 123.

transcript_facts.fact: Patient reports having panic attacks 'out of nowhere'.
Symptoms of panic attacks include heart racing, inability to breathe, and hand tingling.
Panic attacks have been occurring for about four months, since the start of summer.
Frequency of attacks is two or three times a week now, and they are getting worse.
Each panic attack lasts about ten minutes, but the patient feels wiped out afterward.
Patient avoids supermarkets and will not get on the Underground.
Relative states that the patient used to love going into town.
Patient worries about everything else, including work and money.
Patient reports sleep is okay and they get off to sleep fine.
Patient describes their mood as 'a bit fed up, but not depressed'.
Patient denies having any thoughts of harming themselves or ending their life.
Patient reports consuming about four coffees a day, but six if they count the ones at work.
Patient consumes a couple of glasses of wine at the weekend.
Patient confirms no drug use.
Patient works in marketing and has not had any time off.
Relative states they are off at the moment with stress and that work has been awful.
Patient denies problems with heart or thyroid, and the clinician confirms the thyroid was normal last month.
Patient confirms no allergies.
Examination findings show GAD-7 score of 15 and PHQ-9 score of 8, fitting with significant anxiety and panic disorder rather than depression.
The treatment with the best evidence for panic disorder is talking therapy called CBT.
Clinician suggests trying an SSRI called sertraline alongside therapy.
Medication plan: Start Sertraline at 25 mg once a day for one week, then increase to 50 mg once a day.
Follow-up plan: Clinician requests a review in two weeks to see how the patient is getting on with the medication.
Clinician suggests gradually cutting down on coffee.
Safety-netting instruction: If thoughts of self-harm occur, call NHS 111 (mental health option) or Samaritans on 116 123.
